back: A process that uses sample statistics to test a claim about a population parameter.
We start by assuming the null hypothesis is true, then determine if sample data provide enough evidence to reject it.
A statistical hypothesis that contains a statement of equality: $ = $, $ \le $, or $ \ge $.
It is assumed true until evidence suggests otherwise.
Example: $ H_0: \mu = 50 $.
The complement of the null hypothesis. Contains $ \neq $, $ > $, or $ < $.
It represents the claim we are trying to find evidence for.
Example: $ H_a: \mu < 50 $.

cards.front: A car dealership claims the mean oil change time is less than 15 minutes. Write $ H_0 $ and $ H_a $.
back: Claim: $ \mu < 15 $. Complement: $ \mu \ge 15 $.
Complement contains equality → $ H_0: \mu \ge 15 $.
$ H_a: \mu < 15 $ (claim).
Rejecting the null hypothesis when it is actually [[imp:true]].
Probability = $ \alpha $, the level of significance.
Example: Concluding a parachute failure rate > 1% when it's actually ≤ 1%.
Failing to reject the null hypothesis when it is actually [[imp:false]].
Probability = $ \beta $.
Example: Concluding a parachute failure rate ≤ 1% when it's actually > 1%.
The maximum allowable probability of making a [[imp:Type I error]].
Set by the researcher before the test.
They are [[imp:inversely related]]. Decreasing $ \alpha $ reduces the chance of a Type I error but increases the chance of a Type II error (all else equal).
The power of a test is $ 1 - \beta $.
The probability of obtaining a sample statistic as extreme as (or more extreme than) the one observed, assuming $ H_0 $ is true.
A small P-value indicates strong evidence against $ H_0 $.

cards.front: How do you decide whether to reject $ H_0 $ using a P-value?
back: If P-value $ \le \alpha $ → [[imp:reject $ H_0 $]].
If P-value $ > \alpha $ → [[imp:fail to reject $ H_0 $]].
Never say 'accept $ H_0 $'.
The $ > $ symbol indicates a [[kw:right-tailed test]].
The P-value is the area to the right of the test statistic.
cards.front: Identify the type of test: $ H_a: \mu > 100 $.

back: The $ \neq $ symbol indicates a [[kw:two-tailed test]].
The P-value is twice the area in the tail beyond the test statistic.
cards.front: Identify the type of test: $ H_a: p \neq 0.5 $.

back: There is [[imp:enough evidence to reject the claim]].
Example: School claims 61% participation. Reject $ H_0 $ → claim is rejected.
cards.front: If a claim is the null hypothesis and we reject $ H_0 $, what is the conclusion?

back: There is [[imp:not enough evidence to support the claim]].
Example: Dealership claims oil change < 15 min. Fail to reject $ H_0 $ → not enough evidence to support.
cards.front: If a claim is the alternative hypothesis and we fail to reject $ H_0 $, what is the conclusion?

back: Make it [[imp:$ H_a $]] to support the claim.
$ H_0: \mu \ge 96 $, $ H_a: \mu < 96 $ (claim).
If we reject $ H_0 $, we have evidence to support the claim.
cards.front: You want to support a claim that the mean recovery time is less than 96 hours. Should the claim be $ H_0 $ or $ H_a $?
